title: GBE Founder Cory Paddock- Great Traders Know When a Regime Change Is Coming

meta.source: General Transcripts/GBE Founder Cory Paddock- Great Traders Know When a Regime Change Is Coming.docx

speakers: Cory Paddock (founder and CEO, GBE, discretionary power/energy trading firm)
summary: Oct 2025 interview with a US power trader: power as an economics-plus-physics market where a few big setups make the year, edge comes from seeing structural paradigm shifts (coal to gas, wind and solar, data-centre demand) before the market, and history is recency-biased; also hiring, incentive design and trading own capital.

coverage.note: power market nature, chunky P&L, deregulation
data sources, edge vs equities, paradigm-shift edge
history recency bias, coal to gas, wind/solar, demand growth, uncorrelated returns
rising supply and demand volatility, staying ahead
nothing actionable: hiring young talent, outliers
culture, explaining losses, screens identical on own capital
PJM West Hub contract design, P&L swings
few trades make the year, no forced setups, incentive alignment
put option incentive, certainty of pay, motivation

completeness_estimate: 0.92 - short, mostly non-quantitative interview; first reader captured nearly all market and risk ideas, missing only the deregulation history and Cory's reply on variance-seeking traders; no errors found.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: power is very much this this intersection of of economics and and physics
claims.claim: Power trading is a market built on both economics and physical grid constraints, a partly artificial construct with no perfect market design, which creates opportunities because few understand the details.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: somewhere between five and 10 trades make up for the majority of your year
claims.claim: Power P&L is chunky and volatile with five to ten trades making most of the year, so no monthly profit target is sensible.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: they're they're also like excellent at hallucinating
claims.claim: LLMs help digest thousands of pages of market rules and train juniors but hallucinate and can be talked into agreeing with a wrong position, so a domain expert must correct them.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: tick by tick um grid level data uh on the generation side on the power flow side
claims.claim: Power traders use five-minute and tick-level grid data on generation, power flow and nodal prices, not just prices, and years of accumulated pattern recognition.
claims.indicator: nodal prices, generation, power flow, 5-minute data

claims.speaker: Interviewer (Odds on Open host)
claims.quote: it's much harder to have edge there
claims.claim: Equities are hard to find edge in because information (supply chains, customers) is public to everyone, whereas power has dispersed, hard-to-find information.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: having a a point of view on a paradigm shift
claims.claim: The main source of edge is holding a view on a fundamental paradigm shift (where power will flow, surplus and deficiency) before the market, which is still trading the previous paradigm.
claims.conditions: supply and demand constantly change; power amplified
claims.testable: partly - needs identification of shifts ex-ante

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: four sets of eyes on kind of all the same data
claims.claim: Two traders trading the same product with the same data reduces missed information and forces discussion of what each sees.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: we're happy to take the other side of that trade
claims.claim: Historical analysis of 8-10 year old power data gives recency-biased insight because grid topology and price formation change dramatically; trades built on it are ones to fade.
claims.direction: fade trades based on stale historical patterns
claims.testable: yes - test stability of power price relationships over time

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: all the power flows were set up to deliver coal fire coal fired electricity to to load centers
claims.claim: When gas replaced coal, power flows built for coal plants reversed and shifted, producing downstream price effects the market did not predict.
claims.conditions: fuel switch from coal to gas
claims.testable: yes - basis between nodes after plant relocation

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: at first you know we would see a lot of negative prices that has largely gone away
claims.claim: Wind (and later solar) introduction initially created negative prices because operators did not know how to optimize for it, offering opportunities that faded as operators adapted.
claims.conditions: early period of new supply technology

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: for the first time in in my career, we're seeing demand go up
claims.claim: After years of flat or falling power demand (efficiency, offshoring), demand is rising due to data centers, industrialization, EVs and heat pumps, a new paradigm for power prices.
claims.conditions: data centers main driver; EV and heat pump slower than expected

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: power returns so uncorrelated to what's happening in equities
claims.claim: Power returns depend largely on weather and are uncorrelated with equities.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: demand volatility is is going up and then supply supply volatility is also going up
claims.claim: Both demand volatility and supply volatility (wind and solar penetration) are rising, a new paradigm in which the edge is to see changes early and pivot quickly.
claims.testable: yes - realized vol of power prices

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: there's nothing more frustrating than losing money and then not knowing why
claims.claim: Give traders a platform of grid fundamentals so that losses can be explained after the fact and ideas nudged back on track.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: we didn't cut a single corner in ensuring that our screens looked the same
claims.claim: When moving from a firm to own capital, keep identical information and screens so the only change is risk, not reduced information.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: it's actually a weighted average of all the five minute prices within houring 8 to 23 of that particular day
claims.claim: The PJM West Hub balance-of-day product is a weighted average of several nodes and five-minute prices from hour 8 to 23, so part is quasi-settled and the remaining uncertainty is concentrated in the rest of the day.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: a position can can go like instantly for you or against you within a five minute period
claims.claim: Power P&L can swing within five minutes because prices are set in real time, creating a stressful position-sizing environment.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: accumulate like future learning that you can apply to a big setup and that have have the capital behind you to to throw to throw at that setup
claims.claim: Most trades are for learning and staying in the market; the goal is to preserve capital and knowledge to size up on the rare big setup.
claims.direction: size up on rare high-conviction setups

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: the worst thing you can do is like try to force a set that's not there
claims.claim: Lean years occur even with good trading because setups are absent; forcing trades without a setup is the worst mistake.

claims.speaker: Interviewer (Odds on Open host)
claims.quote: obviously assuming you can always keep your job the optimal strategy to maximize your earnings is to go for the highest volatility highest variance approaches
claims.claim: Trader bonuses with no downside make the optimal strategy maximize variance (a free call option), so incentives must penalize losses.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: set up a bit of a put option within every within everybody's um uh incentive structure
claims.claim: The firm adds a put-option-like loss feature to trader compensation to limit blowups, imperfectly, and removes uncertainty about getting paid.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: power trading uh itself um is a relatively new construct. Um really only going back to the uh very tail end of the '9s, early 2000s
claims.claim: Traded US power markets only date from late-1990s/early-2000s deregulation (alongside gas), so market designs are still evolving and usable price histories are short.

claims.speaker: Cory Paddock
claims.quote: the market doesn't really really reward people in the long run that um that go trying those strategies.
claims.claim: Traders who chase maximum variance because their bonus has no downside are not rewarded by the market over the long run, so screening for that mindset matters as much as pay design.
